statement: There is an adapted increasing family (µt)0≤t≤∞ of locally finite measures on H, starting at zero, with the following properties. Its terminal measure is nonatomic and has moments of every integer order on compact sets. Almost surely, simultaneously for all 0 ≤ v < t < ∞, the increment µt − µv is carried by γ([v, t]) ∩ H. The process is locally continuous in total variation, and µt ↑ µ∞ as t → ∞. For every stopping time S, possibly infinite, E [︁ µ∞(dx) − µS(dx) | FS ]︁ = GS(x) dA(x), G∞ := 0. (4.1) This is an equality of conditional measure kernels; in particular it allows nonnegative tests known at time S. Moreover, Eµ∞(dx) = G0(x) dA(x). (4.2)
